name: Down by Law
label: Epitaph
lede: A Boston hardcore lifer, a Los Angeles band, Brett Gurewitz in the parking lot, and a punk cover of a Proclaimers hit that got them on MTV.

eras.title: A side project with a Boston résumé
eras.text: Dave Smalley had already fronted DYS, Dag Nasty and ALL before he started writing songs that didn't fit any of them. In Los Angeles he found guitarist Chris Bagarozzi, bassist Ed Urlik and drummer Dave Naz.

years.h: Smalley starts Down by Law while still in ALL
years.p: [[Dave Smalley|c637a12d-5f55-4b83-bef0-a56b3c1e326c]] wrote "Right or Wrong" during his ALL days and built a band around it with drummer Dave Naz, guitarist Chris Bagarozzi and bassist Ed Urlik.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the band's founding to 1989 and lists Smalley, Bagarozzi, Urlik and Naz as the original four. Smalley told No Echo the band began as a side project while he was still in [[ALL|e92547b5-a134-4149-af9a-c944af9e476f]].

years.cap: Down by Law's first show, per Wikipedia
years.p: Down by Law played its first show at the Anti-Club in Hollywood on March 10, 1990.
years.xp: The band was a Los Angeles unit fronted by a Boston hardcore veteran, a mix that would define its sound: East Coast punk speed with California polish.

eras.title: Epitaph and the Gurewitz records
eras.text: Brett Gurewitz of Bad Religion saw the band live and signed it to Epitaph. Two Gurewitz-produced albums followed before the first lineup came apart.

years.h: Brett Gurewitz signs them after an early show
years.p: Epitaph founder [[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]] took the band out to his car after a show, and Smalley says the next thing he knew Down by Law was on Epitaph.
years.xp: Smalley described the moment to No Echo: Gurewitz brought them out to his car to talk, and the deal followed.

years.p: Twelve songs in about 35 minutes, produced by Brett Gurewitz, including "Right or Wrong," "American Dream" and "Surf Punk" (with music by Ed Urlik).
years.xp: Smalley wrote most of it. Naz wrote "The Truth," and "Best Friends" is a cover of a song by The Outlets.

years.p: The second album, again produced by Brett Gurewitz, arrived the following year on Epitaph.

years.h: The original lineup breaks up, leaving only Smalley
years.p: After touring behind Blue, Bagarozzi, Urlik and Naz left, and Smalley was the last original member.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band parted ways with its original lineup in 1993. The "D.C. Guns" EP also dates from 1993.

eras.title: Punkrockacademyfightsong
eras.text: With Sam Williams, John DiMambro and Hunter Oswald, Down by Law found the lineup and the record that made its name.

years.h: New lineup: Williams, DiMambro and Oswald
years.p: Sam Williams on guitar, "Angry" John DiMambro on bass and Hunter Oswald on drums join Dave Smalley to form the band's second lineup.
Recorded at A&M Studios in Hollywood with producer Michael W. Douglass, and generally cited as the band's best seller.
years.xp: The album includes a punk take on The Proclaimers' "I'm Gonna Be (500 Miles)," which got MTV and radio play, as did the video for "Hit or Miss." Smalley told No Echo an unspoken electricity was in the room while they made it.

years.h: Recording next door to the Rolling Stones
years.p: Wikipedia says the Stones were recording at A&M at the same time and allegedly complained about how loud the punk band was.

eras.title: Touring machine, then a new label
eras.text: Down by Law spent these years on the road with the big Epitaph and Fat bands, made two more Epitaph albums, and then left for Go-Kart.

years.h: Smalley juggles fatherhood and graduate school
years.p: Smalley says he toured full time while studying at Cal State Los Angeles, using its quarter system to fit in three-month tours, and that becoming a father in 1995 changed how he toured.
years.xp: He told No Echo the schedule bent around school terms and then around family.

years.p: The fourth album, and the first one after Hunter Oswald's first stint on drums ended in 1996.

years.h: Last of the Sharpshooters, the last Epitaph album
years.p: Down by Law's final record for Epitaph before it moved to Go-Kart.

years.h: On the road with NOFX, The Offspring, Pennywise and Bad Religion
years.p: Wikipedia lists those bands among the acts Down by Law supported during the 1990s.
The band departed the label it had been on since 1991 to sign with Go-Kart Records.
The band's one album for Go-Kart Records, after which John DiMambro and drummer Chris Lagerborg left.

eras.title: Rebuilding, a loss, a hiatus
eras.text: The lineup turned over again, the band changed labels again, and by 2003 it went quiet.

years.h: Split with Pseudo Heroes; Milo Todesco takes the drums
years.p: Down by Law shared a 2000 split release with Pseudo Heroes, with Keith Davies on bass and Milo Todesco on drums after the Fly the Flag departures.

years.h: Former drummer Chris Lagerborg dies at 33
years.p: Wikipedia reports that Lagerborg, who left after Fly the Flag, died in his sleep in 2002.
The band signed to Union 2112 in December 2002 and released the album in May 2003.
Down by Law went on hiatus later in 2003.

eras.title: Back on the road, and the 1994 lineup returns
eras.text: Smalley restarted the band in 2008 and kept it going, and by 2017 the Punkrockacademyfightsong lineup was back together.

years.h: Down by Law returns with new material
years.p: The band came back in August 2008 after five years away.

years.h: First tour since 2003, including South America
years.p: Down by Law played South America and some US shows in 2009.
The first full album of the reunion era.
John DiMambro and Hunter Oswald came back, reuniting the lineup that made Punkrockacademyfightsong.
The first album with the 1994 lineup restored.
A 2021 album from the reunited lineup.
Released July 12, 2024, the band's newest album.
